screens.reason: The section is well grouped and the error banner leads straight to Change password, but two folder ideas with near-identical names sit in one block.

findings.problem: Under 'Folders shown and synchronised' the toggle 'Show only subscribed folders' and the column 'Synchronised in the background' read as the same thing. A project manager does not know what 'subscribed' means or how it differs from 'synchronised'.
findings.fix: Rename the toggle to 'Hide folders I switched off on the mail server' and keep 'synchronised' as the only term for the table, with the existing explanation line directly under the heading.

findings.problem: The 'Settings for mailbox' field has no arrow here, while the same field in Signatures, Automatic reply and Delegation has one. It reads as plain text, so a person with two mailboxes does not see they can switch.
findings.fix: Draw the mailbox selector identically in every per-mailbox section, with the arrow.

findings.problem: 'Open mailto links in this app' and the version line with 'Copy version' apply to the whole app, yet they sit under a selector that says the section is per mailbox.
findings.fix: Move both below a divider labelled 'For the whole app', or move the mailto toggle to Appearance.

screens.reason: Three tables with clear headings, but the sender address table does not fit its width and the row actions collide with the text beside them.

findings.problem: In 'Sender addresses' the links 'Rename' and 'Delete' overlap the reply-to text of the alias rows ('team@northwind-projects.testRename') and 'Delete' runs past the right edge of the dialog. The sender name field also cuts 'Olivia Brandt, Nort'.
findings.fix: Put reply-to and blind copy on a second line under the address, widen the sender name field, and keep the actions in a column of their own inside the dialog.

findings.problem: The sender name is an editable field in the row and there is also a 'Rename' link, so there are two ways to change a name and it is unclear what 'Rename' renames (the name or the address).
findings.fix: Drop the inline field or the link: either a row that opens for editing through 'Edit', or inline fields with only 'Delete' as action.

findings.problem: The heading says 'Sender addresses', the text says 'sender identities', the button says 'Add alias' and the navigation says 'sender names'. Four words for one thing.
findings.fix: Pick one term, for example 'sender address', and use it in the navigation label, heading, description and button ('Add sender address').

findings.problem: In the open 'Insert variable' menu the mail address value runs out of the menu on the right. The 'Text blocks' table is on this section although the navigation label does not mention text blocks.
findings.fix: Wrap or shorten the value in the menu, and give text blocks one home (see the finding across screens).

screens.reason: On its own this is the clearest screen of the pack, but the same automatic reply is drawn a second time, with other dates, in the Rules section.

findings.problem: This section sets an automatic reply from 12 to 16 October with subject 'Out of office until Friday 16 October', while the Rules section shows an 'Away reply' card for the same mailbox from 19 to 23 October with another subject. A person cannot tell which one is sent.
findings.fix: Keep the reply only in this section and replace the card in Rules with one line 'Automatic reply is on until Friday 16 October' and a link to here.

findings.problem: Under 'Schedule' the option 'Between two dates' is chosen, yet the weekly option below it shows Sat and Sun selected and hours filled in. It looks as if both schedules apply.
findings.fix: Grey out or collapse the fields of the option that is not chosen, or draw the weekly choice as a second frame.

screens.reason: Each group has one question, a plain heading and a one-line explanation, and the layout pictures show the result.

findings.problem: 'Replies', 'Default send button' and 'Play a sound when a message has been sent' are about writing and sending, not about how the app looks. Someone looking for them would not open 'Appearance'.
findings.fix: Rename the navigation label and title to 'Appearance and behaviour', or put the three groups under a subheading 'Writing and sending'.

screens.reason: The rules table reads well as when and then, but the section opens with a second away reply and shows two buttons that run the rules.

findings.problem: The 'Away reply' card at the top is a second copy of the Automatic reply section, with other dates and another subject, and its subject ('Away until Monday 26 October') does not match its own end date of Friday 23 October.
findings.fix: Remove the editable card here and show a one-line status with a link to the Automatic reply section. Move 'Follow the absence in my profile' and the formatted and plain text variants to that section.

findings.problem: Next to the heading 'Rules for incoming mail' there is a button 'Run on a folder now', and right under it a strip 'Run the rules over the mail already in' with a folder field and 'Run now'. Two controls for one action, and the first has no folder to act on.
findings.fix: Keep the strip with the folder field and 'Run now', and remove the button 'Run on a folder now' from the heading row.

findings.problem: The condition 'Header List-Unsubscribe is present' in the Newsletters row is a technical term a project manager does not know.
findings.fix: Show it as 'Is a newsletter or mailing list' and keep the header name in a tooltip or the edit form.

findings.problem: The section holds four things (away reply, forwarding, rules, quick actions) under the name 'Rules'. 'Quick actions' are started by hand and are not rules. The mailbox selector text touches the field edge without an arrow.
findings.fix: Give quick actions their own navigation entry or a tab inside this section, and draw the selector as in the other sections.

screens.reason: Each block is clear, but the section is a mix of four subjects and one of them has nothing to do with search or cleaning up.

findings.problem: The block 'Invitations' ('Add incoming invitations to the calendar as tentative') sits under 'Search and clean-up', where nobody looks for a calendar setting.
findings.fix: Move it to the Appearance and behaviour section or to a small 'Calendar' group, and keep this section to search, trash and spam.

findings.problem: 'Include message bodies when searching the priority inbox' uses 'priority inbox' as if known. The administration calls the same idea 'Sort by importance'.
findings.fix: Use one name for it in both places and add half a sentence here on what the priority inbox is on first mention.

findings.problem: The blocked senders list lives here, while the list of trusted senders and the 'external' marking live under Privacy and security. A person looking for 'who do I block or trust' has to know two places.
findings.fix: Put blocked senders next to the trusted senders in Privacy and security, or link from one list to the other.

screens.reason: The two delegation tables are understandable, but half of the section is about text blocks, which already have a table in another section.

findings.problem: 'My text blocks' and 'Text blocks shared with me' are on the Delegation section, while the Signatures section has its own 'Text blocks' table with other names (Demo invitation, Hours reminder against Demo follow-up, Rollout kick-off agenda). A person cannot tell if these are the same list.
findings.fix: Make one 'Text blocks' section in the navigation with the columns name, text, shared with and the actions edit, share and delete, and remove the tables from Signatures and Delegation.

findings.problem: In 'Accounts I may act for' the first row shows 'Open beside my own' as a small outlined mark under the name, and the second row shows the same words as a button. It is not clear that the first means 'is open' and the second 'open it'.
findings.fix: Use a toggle 'Shown beside my own mailbox' in both rows, or show 'Opened' as text with a 'Close' button against 'Open beside my own' as the button.

findings.problem: 'Insert' on 'Text blocks shared with me' has nothing to insert into: the settings dialog is open and no message is being written.
findings.fix: Replace 'Insert' here by 'Preview' or 'Copy to my text blocks', and leave inserting to the writing window.

findings.problem: The grey strip with the 'From' selector ('Marieke de Vries, sent by Olivia Brandt') has no label of its own and sits between two tables, so it is not clear which account it is about.
findings.fix: Give it a heading 'How mail from a delegated account is signed' and state the account it applies to, or move the choice into the row of that account.

screens.reason: Two groups, plain labels and a one-line explanation under every choice.

findings.problem: The form 'New name for this device' under the table does not say which row it belongs to. 'This device' is also the mark on the Firefox row, while the value is 'Olivia's iPhone'.
findings.fix: Open the name field inside the row being renamed, or title the form 'New name for Mail app on iPhone'.

findings.problem: 'Sign out' suggests the person is logged out of mail on that device, while the text says it only stops notifications there.
findings.fix: Rename the button to 'Stop notifications' if that is all it does, or say in the description that the device is also signed out of mail.

screens.reason: Import first and export last is a logical order, but the row buttons in the Imports table use four different verbs without saying what each one stops.

findings.problem: In the 'Imports' table 'Pause' and 'Resume' appear on imports that are already 'Done'. They pause the recurring check of the old account, not the import, and that is only readable from the small grey line.
findings.fix: Rename them to 'Pause checking' and 'Resume checking'.

findings.problem: Stopping is called 'Abort' in 'Upload in progress', 'Cancel and delete' in the table and 'Remove from list' next to it. A first-time user cannot tell which of these throws away imported mail.
findings.fix: Use 'Cancel upload', 'Cancel and delete imported mail' and 'Remove from list', and repeat the consequence in a confirmation.

findings.problem: The form shows 'Another account over IMAP' chosen, while 'Upload in progress' shows a PST file and the table shows a running IMAP import. Three states in one picture make it unclear what the person just did.
findings.fix: Draw the screen as frames: a new import being filled in, b upload in progress, c the list of imports.

findings.problem: The status message 'Import running, 1,240 of 2,000 messages' sits right beside the close button of the dialog and half over its top edge.
findings.fix: Place the status in the header row of the section or as the first line of the 'Imports' block.

screens.reason: Every toggle says what happens when it is off, and the certificate tables explain S/MIME in one sentence.

findings.problem: 'Certificate per account and alias' lists the aliases o.brandt@northwind.example and noreply@northwind-projects.test, while the Signatures section lists delivery@ and olivia.brandt@ as the aliases of the same mailbox.
findings.fix: Use the same set of addresses for this mailbox on both sections.

findings.problem: This section has no 'Settings for mailbox' selector although certificates are assigned per account and alias, and it mixes app-wide toggles with per-address choices.
findings.fix: State in the intro line 'These settings apply to every mailbox', as Appearance does.

screens.reason: A list with one main action is right, but the picture shows the list, an open 'New domain' form and an open detail panel at once, and the form hides the table.

findings.problem: The 'New domain' form covers the intro text, the column headings for mailboxes and storage, and the values of the first two rows. With the detail panel of another domain open at the same time, it is unclear which domain the page is about.
findings.fix: Split into frames: a the list alone, b the list with the detail panel, c the 'New domain' form as a dialog over the dimmed page.

findings.problem: The detail panel repeats the DNS records, the warning and 'Check DNS records now' of the domain page, with the state called 'Found' here and 'Correct' there. There is no visible link from the panel to the domain page with its General and Signatures tabs.
findings.fix: Keep the panel as a short summary with one button 'Open domain', and use one state word in both places.

findings.problem: The second intro line 'One console for every record of the mail service, apart from the mail rules and integrations' does not help an administrator and competes with the first.
findings.fix: Remove the second line.

screens.reason: Three clear cards with good explanations, but 'Sign-in' and 'Limits' also exist on other administration pages with other values in view.

findings.problem: The card 'Limits' sets 'Size of one upload' to 25 MB, while Protection has 'Largest message' 25 MB and Settings has 'Largest attachment' 25 MB. An administrator cannot tell which of the three wins.
findings.fix: Keep message and attachment size on Protection under 'Limits', and here show only 'Storage for uploads not yet sent' with a link to the size limit.

findings.problem: The card 'Sign-in' sets the sign-on provider here, while Settings has a tab 'People and sign-in' with the directory, Google and Microsoft sign-in.
findings.fix: Put all sign-in settings in one place and link to it from the other.

findings.problem: The intro says 'Changes apply at once', yet the page ends with 'Save changes' and 'Discard'.
findings.fix: Change the sentence to 'Changes apply as soon as you save, nobody is signed out'.

screens.reason: The DNS tab is exemplary (what each record does, state, one action), but the other tabs do not show how a change is saved.

findings.problem: Frame b (General) has toggles, a 'Deliver to' field and a storage field but no save button, while the Mail server and Protection pages save with a button. It is unclear whether typing 100 GB takes effect.
findings.fix: Add the same 'Save changes' and 'Discard' row as on the other pages, or state under the tab that each change is saved at once.

findings.problem: In frame a the red block 'Delete everything the server holds about the people of this domain' sits under the DNS tab after a large empty gap, as if it belongs to DNS.
findings.fix: Move the block to the General tab under a heading 'Danger zone', or place it directly under the tab card on every tab.

findings.problem: In frame b the administrators table removes a person with a bare cross, including the workspace administrator Ines Okafor who cannot be removed from one domain.
findings.fix: Label the action 'Remove' and leave it out on rows inherited from the whole server.

findings.problem: Frame c calls it 'Forced on every message' and 'Forced signature', while the person sees 'Made mandatory by the domain administrator' in their own settings.
findings.fix: Use 'mandatory' in both places.

screens.reason: The list, tabs and dialogs follow one pattern, but passwords are handled in a way that contradicts what the same screens say about sign-in.

findings.problem: Frame b says a personal mailbox 'signs in with the workspace account', yet frame c hands out a temporary mailbox password and the row menu in frame a offers 'Reset password'. The mailbox page of a person says the password lives with the workspace sign-on. An administrator cannot tell whether a mailbox has its own password.
findings.fix: Decide per sign-in mode: with single sign-on leave out frame c and name the menu item 'Reset password in the workspace', and show the temporary password only when the server has its own passwords, with that condition in the caption.

findings.problem: In frame a the open row menu covers the last sign-in and the menu button of five rows, and it hangs above the row of Tom Achterberg it belongs to.
findings.fix: Open the menu on a row with free space below it, for example the second row.

findings.problem: 'Message everyone' next to 'New mailbox' does not say who everyone is (46 mailboxes of this domain or the tab in view) or what kind of message.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Send a message to all 46 mailboxes' or move it into a menu with that explanation.

findings.problem: 'Close to storage limit 3' and 'Not signed in for 30 days' look like buttons, not filters, and 'Reserved address prefixes' has a settings icon but opens a dialog about addresses.
findings.fix: Put the word 'Show' before the two filters and draw them as selectable chips with an on state.

screens.reason: Five tabs divide the person well, but the Folders tab has two destructive buttons without a label and the Addresses tab uses three overlapping terms.

findings.problem: In frame c every folder row ends with a bin icon and a boxed cross, with no label. The note below says one empties the folder and one deletes it, but not which is which, and both appear on Inbox, which cannot be deleted.
findings.fix: Use text buttons 'Empty' and 'Delete folder', and leave out 'Delete folder' on Inbox, Drafts, Sent, Spam and Trash.

findings.problem: Frame a has three tables, 'Extra addresses', 'Sender addresses this person may use' and 'Sender identities', and the person calls the same things 'alias' and 'sender address' in their own settings.
findings.fix: Merge to one table of addresses with the columns address, kind (main, extra, shared, group), sender name and may send, and use the term the person sees.

findings.problem: Frame c has a column 'Subscribed' with Yes or No and a button 'Subscribe to all folders'. The term is not explained and is called 'synchronised' or 'shown' elsewhere.
findings.fix: Rename the column to 'Shown in the folder list' and the button to 'Show all folders'.

findings.problem: Frame d calls it 'Away reply' with 'From' and 'Until', while the person's section is called 'Automatic reply' with 'Starts' and 'Ends'. The same dates and nearly the same text appear in a third form.
findings.fix: Call it 'Automatic reply' everywhere with the same field names, and keep 'Filter script' as the only other item on this tab.

screens.reason: Three tabs for three questions with plain words for technical ideas, and only a few button names leave doubt.

findings.problem: In frame b the right panel offers 'Retry sending' and 'Reprocess' side by side. 'Reprocess' is only mentioned in passing inside the error text and is not in the row.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Run through the rules again' with a tooltip, or put one line under the buttons saying what each does.

findings.problem: In frame a 'Remove matching mail' sits next to the primary button and acts on the filter typed in the search field. It is easy to miss that it deletes three messages for good.
findings.fix: Show the count in the button ('Remove 3 matching messages') and place it under the filter result line.

findings.problem: The tabs here are in sentence case with a counter, while Domains, Mailboxes and the mailbox page use capital-letter tabs.
findings.fix: Use one tab style on all administration pages.

findings.problem: In frame c the retention setting 'Deleted mail stays recoverable for' with its own 'Save' sits above the search form, while the Assistant page offers export of the same deleted mail per person.
findings.fix: Keep retention here and move the per-person export of deleted mail to this tab as a button next to 'Restore 2 selected messages'.

screens.reason: The status table answers 'is it working' at a glance, but below it six blocks compete and the maintenance table cuts off the one column that explains each job.

findings.problem: In the 'Maintenance' table the column 'What it does' is cut off on every row ('Builds the search index agai…', 'Finds messages, folders and…') and the scope fields cut their value ('Customers / Kassel, C', '18 people follow their p'). An administrator has to start a job without being able to read what it does or on what.
findings.fix: Give the Maintenance table the full page width, with the explanation on a second line under the job name and wider scope fields.

findings.problem: The page holds status, self-test, operations log, connections, maintenance jobs and running tasks. Only the first is 'health'.
findings.fix: Use tabs as on Queues and recovery: 'Status' (status table, self-test, connected now), 'Maintenance' (jobs and running tasks side by side), and 'Operations log'.

findings.problem: In 'Connected right now' each row ends with a bare power icon, and the client and address columns are cut ('Mail in the bro…', '145.27.88.3, h…'). The same action is called 'Cut off all sessions' on the mailbox page.
findings.fix: Use a text button 'Cut off' and widen the client column.

findings.problem: In 'Running tasks' the buttons are 'Cancel', 'Remove' and 'Report' without saying what is removed or reported.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Cancel task', 'Remove from queue' and 'Open report'.

screens.reason: The settings are named by what they do instead of by their technical name, which is rare and good, but the page is long, one row is broken and a heading is used twice.

findings.problem: In the row 'Send all outgoing mail through one relay server' the label 'Username' is printed over the port field, and the relay server address is cut off.
findings.fix: Put the four fields on two lines (server and port, username and password) with a wider server field.

findings.problem: 'Connections' is both a row inside the card 'Limits' (how many at once) and the title of the third card (encryption).
findings.fix: Rename the row to 'Connections at the same time' and the card to 'Encryption and relay'.

findings.problem: Save and discard are at the top right of a page of about three screens, while the Mail server page has them at the bottom. After changing the last setting no button is in view.
findings.fix: Use a save row that stays in view at the bottom on every administration page.

findings.problem: The card 'Limits' has nine rows of numbers in one list, from message size to commands per minute.
findings.fix: Split it into 'Message size' (largest message, recipients, headers) and 'Rates' (connections, commands, per sender, per recipient, per user), or make the three cards tabs.

screens.reason: Rules in plain when and then sentences with an editor that mirrors them, but the box above the table reads as a setting while it is a test.

findings.problem: The box 'Rewrite rules that apply to this address' with a field and 'Show rules' looks like a setting or a filter of the table. It is a test that shows which rules touch one address.
findings.fix: Title it 'Test an address', rename the button to 'Test', and place it under the table or behind a button next to 'Add rule'.

findings.problem: The page does not say how these rules relate to the rules a person makes in their own settings or to the filter script on the mailbox page: which runs first.
findings.fix: Add one line to the intro: 'These run for everyone, before a person's own rules'.

findings.problem: In the editor the open menu 'What should happen' is drawn under two actions that are already chosen, and 'Combine conditions with and, or and not' does not show how to change AND into OR.
findings.fix: Make the words AND, OR and NOT in front of each condition visibly selectable, and draw the menu as a separate frame.

screens.reason: One list for three kinds of integration with a panel per kind works, but pausing is offered three times and the list cuts off its key columns.

findings.problem: In frame a 'Pause' is a button in every row under a column titled 'Pause or resume', again in the panel footer, and the row also has a menu button. Three ways to do one thing in view.
findings.fix: Keep the state as a toggle in the row and remove 'Pause' from the panel footer, or keep it only in the panel.

findings.problem: In frame c the button under the API key is called 'Regenerate secret', the word the webhook panel uses for another thing. The line beside it says 'Replaces the key'.
findings.fix: Call it 'Regenerate key' on API keys.

findings.problem: The columns 'Integration' and 'Where' are cut off in every row ('OpenProject, linked co…', 'Sends as billing@no…'), while the panel takes a third of the width.
findings.fix: Drop the separate pause column to give 'Where' the room, or wrap to two lines.

findings.problem: The page title 'Webhooks and API' leaves out website forms, and the group heading 'Fires at' in the panel is jargon.
findings.fix: Title the page 'Integrations' as the button 'Add integration' already does, and rename 'Fires at' to 'When to send'.

screens.reason: The page is a rest drawer: most of what it holds has a named home on another administration page, sometimes with the same value under another name.

findings.problem: Frame a has 'Largest attachment 25 MB' under 'Server configuration', 'Standard quota 10 GB per mailbox' under 'Storage' and 'Check server certificates'. The Mail server page, Protection and the domain page set the same things under other names.
findings.fix: Remove 'Server configuration' and 'Storage' from this tab and link to Protection (sizes, certificates) and Domains (quota). Keep here only what has no other page: defaults for new users, product features, custom fields.

findings.problem: Frame b 'People and sign-in' holds the directory, admitted groups and Google and Microsoft sign-in, while the Mail server page holds the 'Sign-in' card with the sign-on provider. 'Administrators of this server' repeats the administrators table of the domain page.
findings.fix: Make one page 'People and sign-in' in the navigation that holds the sign-in card of Mail server, the directory, the groups and all administrators with their scope.

findings.problem: None of the four tabs shows a save button, while fields such as 'Connection timeout', 'Directory address' and the client secrets clearly need one.
findings.fix: Add the shared save row of the other administration pages.

findings.problem: 'Mail templates, shared templates for replies' is what people call 'text blocks', 'Sort by importance' is their 'priority inbox', and 'Language model features' is the 'Assistant' that has its own page. In frame d 'A master password' against 'A master user that may open every mailbox' is a heavy choice with no explanation.
findings.fix: Use the person-facing names, move the language model toggle to the Assistant page, and add one line per sign-in option on what it means for security.

screens.reason: Three unrelated subjects share one page under the navigation label 'Assistant', and the largest one, working in a person's mailbox, belongs to the mailbox page.

findings.problem: The card 'People's mailboxes' (who may open an account, export deleted mail, restore from an archive file) is under 'Assistant'. An administrator looks for it on the page of that person under Mailboxes, which has tabs but none for this, and under Queues and recovery.
findings.fix: Move 'Who may open this account' to a tab 'Access' on the mailbox page, and the export and restore blocks to the Recovery tab or a tab 'Recovery' on the mailbox page.

findings.problem: The page ends with 'Save' and 'Cancel' for assistant, language and look, while 'Grant access', 'Withdraw', 'Export deleted mail' and 'Restore mail' in the right card act at once. It is unclear what 'Cancel' undoes.
findings.fix: After the move above the save row covers only settings. Until then, put the save row inside the left column.

findings.problem: 'Language and look' (default language, colours, logo) has nothing to do with the assistant and is not findable from the navigation.
findings.fix: Move it to Settings as a tab 'Language and look', and bring the toggle 'Language model features for the whole server' from Settings to this page.

findings.problem: The access table uses 'May' with 'Read, reply and file' and 'Withdraw', while the shared mailbox dialog uses 'Access' with 'Read and send' and a cross, and the person's own settings use 'Full access' and 'Take away'.
findings.fix: Use one set of access levels and one verb for removing access in all three places.

across.problem: The automatic reply exists as its own settings section, as an 'Away reply' card in Rules, as 'Away reply' on the administrator's Rules tab and as 'Rewrite automatic replies' in maintenance, with two names, different field names and different dates for the same person.
across.fix: Call it 'Automatic reply' everywhere, give the person one place to edit it, and show a read-only status with a link in Rules.

across.problem: Text blocks have a table in Signatures, two tables in Delegation with other content, and are called 'Mail templates' in the administration.
across.fix: One section 'Text blocks' in the settings dialog with sharing included, and the same word in the product features list.

across.problem: Size and storage limits are set on five pages: 'Size of one upload', 'Largest message', 'Largest attachment', and the quota per server, per domain and per person. Three of them show 25 MB under three names.
across.fix: One home for message size (Protection) and one chain for quota (server default on Domains, then domain, then person), each showing where its value comes from.

across.problem: Sign-in is set on Mail server and on Settings, and the mailbox screens disagree on whether a mailbox has a password of its own (temporary password and 'Reset password' against 'her password lives with the workspace sign-on').
across.fix: One page 'People and sign-in', and password actions shown only in the sign-in mode where they exist.

across.problem: Saving follows four patterns: buttons at the bottom (Mail server, Assistant), at the top (Protection), a save per block (Recovery retention, Limits tab) and no button at all (Settings, domain General tab).
across.fix: One save row that stays in view at the bottom of every administration page with fields, and a stated 'saved at once' for toggles in tables.

across.problem: Tabs are in capital letters on the domain, mailboxes and mailbox pages and in sentence case on Queues and recovery and Settings. Removing a row is a bare cross on some tables and a 'Remove' button on others.
across.fix: One tab style and a labelled 'Remove' button in every administration table.

across.problem: Access to someone's mailbox is named three ways: 'Full access' with 'Take away' and 'Give up', 'Read and send' or 'Read only' with a cross, and 'Read, reply and file' with 'Withdraw'.
across.fix: One list of access levels and the verbs 'Grant' and 'Withdraw' in all three places.

across.problem: The signed-in person on most administration pages is Olivia Brandt, the delivery lead who is the ordinary user in the settings dialog, while Mail server, the domain page and the mailbox pages show Ines Okafor, also with the role 'Delivery lead'. It suggests a project manager administers the mail server.
across.fix: Show Ines Okafor with a role such as 'Workspace administrator' on every administration page.

across.problem: Per-mailbox sections start with a 'Settings for mailbox' selector, drawn with an arrow in some and without in others, and app-wide sections say so in a sentence in some (Appearance) and not in others (Privacy, Notifications).
across.fix: Same selector in every per-mailbox section and the same first line 'These settings apply to every mailbox' in every app-wide section.

across.problem: No screen of this pack shows the mark 'Nextcloud only', so its clarity could not be judged here. If any of these controls exist only in Nextcloud, nothing tells the reader.
across.fix: If the mark applies to controls in this pack, place it directly after the label of the control it belongs to.

keep: Settings are named by what they do with the technical term in the explanation, for example 'Delay first-time senders' and the 'What it does' column for MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
Every toggle has one line that says what happens when it is on or off, as in Privacy and security and Appearance.
Destructive actions state the consequence next to the button ('Removing takes this mailbox out of the app. Mail on the server stays where it is.', 'Remove from list keeps them').
The administration follows list, then detail page with breadcrumb and tabs, then dialog (Domains, Mailboxes, one person), and the lettered frames show one state each.
Rules read as 'when' and 'then' sentences in both the personal rules table and the processing rules, with the editor mirroring the same words.
